note: On 110-acre East Twin Lake, five miles north of Clam Lake, in maple, birch and hemlock forest. Sites 5, 8 and 9 sit on the shore with open ground under tall trees to the water; 3 and 7 look at the lake through the trees. Fishing pier; the boat ramp is about half a mile east. A spur trail and township roads link to the Dead Horse Run ATV trail; ATVs may not be ridden in the campground. --Claude
summary: FS page, recreation.gov facility/rates and per-site catalog + photos read. 10 sites (9 drive-in, 1 tent), $15, no hookups, vault toilets + water, 6 reservable/4 FCFS, 14-night max, season (manual) matches. Lakefront KEPT with a caveat naming sites 5, 8, 9 (rec.gov per-site 'Lakefront' tags + photos; canopy hides pads on imagery). max_rig_ft 40 -> 45 (rec.gov). Note rewritten.
flags: WATERFRONT: lakefront KEPT (no change) on a few clear sites - caveat in the note. Imagery is canopy-blind (tall trees over every pad), so per the curation doc the per-site sources decide: recreation.gov tags sites 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 'Lakefront'. The rec.gov photos show site 5 on open leaf-litter ground running ~15 m to the shore with a bench at the water, and sites 8 and 9 with the lake directly behind them through an open-understory pine stand; 3 and 7 show the lake through trees; 6's photo shows no water. Catalog points on Esri imagery: site 5 at 46.19156,-90.85943 (~15 m from the shore), 8 at 46.19125,-90.85860 (~18 m), 9 at 46.19153,-90.85798 (~13 m). 5, 8 and 9 are reservable nightly sites (35/25/40 ft on rec.gov; 30/25/30 ft on the FS page), so all sold by the night and fit a 23-ft rig.

SITE LENGTHS: FS page 'Back in 40 Foot: 1, 2', '30 Foot: 5, 9', '25 Foot: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8' and 'RV's up to 30 feet'; recreation.gov gives 2 = 45, 1 and 9 = 40, 5 and 7 = 35, 3, 4, 6, 8 = 25. Written max_rig_ft 45 per the trust-rec.gov rule; every drive-in site takes 25 ft+ on both sources.

PHONE: stored 715-264-2511 (on recreation.gov as the second of two numbers) -> 715-638-7243 (the FS page's 'Office Contact Information: Hayward Office ... Phone: 715-638-7243'); optional, same as the Day Lake (3350) proposal.
